  7. #5236 — Windows: Entra broker token cache stays 0 bytes after MCP sign-in (OPEN, 5 comments) — Every new process re-prompts for account selection. A meaningful auth friction point for Windows MCP users.

  8. #5354 — ACP doesn't advertise Fusion or tier configuration (OPEN, 👍2, filed yesterday) — Fusion exists interactively but ACP surfaces only "Auto," blocking third-party clients like T3 Code from exposing tier selection. Early signal that the ACP surface is lagging the TUI.

  9. #5151 — Regression: Sol models rejected pre-prompt as tool definitions balloon from 15K to ~260K tokens (OPEN) — compaction_static_context_blocked failures at default context tier since Oct 14. A regression with real impact on default-config users.

  10. #5323 — Allow disabling agent checkpoint refs (refs/agents/*) (OPEN) — Every turn writes checkpoint commits authored under the user's git identity, polluting ref listings. A reasonable ergonomics/compliance request likely to resonate with teams.

4. Key PR Progress

Only one PR was updated in the last 24h:

  • #5186 — Update feature_request.yml (OPEN, by Bilalabdulkadir) — A change to the feature-request issue template, intended to improve triage of incoming feature requests (linked to the repo's "close invalid PR writer" workflow). Low complexity, but relevant to how community feedback is routed.

Note: the repository saw no substantive feature/code PRs in this window; most iteration is arriving via the rapid pre-release cadence.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this period, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Terminal/editor integration: OSC 7501 program-status reporting (#5112, #5320 — 👍17 and 👍8), Kitty inline image rendering (now shipped in -7), markdown rendering in submitted user-message timeline (#5353), and /code to jump into VS Code (shipped).
  • Configurability & opt-outs: enableTelemetry boolean in settings.json (#3387), disabling agent checkpoint refs (#5323), and Fusion tier settings surfacing through ACP (#5354).
  • Agent/skill semantics: making disable-model-invocation mean "manual-only" rather than "unreachable" (#4438), plus better warnings for ignored frontmatter keys (shipped in -8).
  • Platform parity: consistent Windows behavior for local models (auto llama.cpp install, shipped) and MCP/Entra auth caching (#5236).

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Enterprise managed-settings instability is the top frustration — a dense cluster of reports (#5109, #5130, #5341, #5342, #5346) covering refresh retry loops, HTTP 422 "Validation Failed" server-side regressions, "model: Expected string, received object" parse errors, and startup/resume hangs under forceRemoteSettingsRefresh. Users describe the CLI as "unusable" on managed accounts.
  2. Auth/credential persistence on Windows — Entra broker token caches not surviving across processes (#5236), plus historical WSL2 keychain/keyring detection failures (#49).
  3. Model routing/context regressions — Fusion models hanging in plan mode (#5270) and Sol models failing before the first prompt due to oversized static tool definitions (#5151) are eroding trust in default configurations.
  4. Sandbox friction on developer toolchains — macOS sandbox blocking local daemon connections (#5105) and Windows CreateProcessW preflight failures (#5285) show sandbox enforcement still misfires on common setups.
  5. Silent or opaque failures — settings ignored without warning (being fixed in -9), Connectors failing only in interactive mode with debug-level logging (#5347), and bare HTTP 422s when cli_remote_control_enabled is false (#4409).
  6. Windows turn stalls — a fresh report (#5356) of intermittent multi-minute mid-turn hangs requiring cancel/continue adds to platform-stability concerns.
OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode Community Digest — 2026-11-05

Today's Highlights

No releases shipped in the last 24 hours, but the issue tracker is dominated by free-tier quota problems consolidating under issue #59387 (280 comments), plus a cluster of platform-specific reports (Windows desktop losing free limits while mobile works). On the PR side, the dominant theme is a large refactor wave from contributor Hona converting UI subsystems — voice calls, file tree, tabs, disclosures, line comments — into explicit state machines, while kitlangton lands feature-flag registry infrastructure.

Releases

None in the last 24 hours.

Hot Issues

  1. #59387 — [zen] Free tier issues: read this first, then post your report here (280 comments, 20 👍) The canonical free-tier megathread. All "Free usage exceeded," counter-reset-never-happens, and desktop "no longer supported" reports funnel here. Volume alone makes it the health barometer for OpenCode's free offering; the pinned-issue pattern is working but the underlying problem clearly isn't resolved.

  2. #50155 — [CLOSED] opencode-go: DeepSeek V4 Flash requires Global regions but Privacy setting is missing (21 comments, 15 👍) Paid Go subscribers blocked by an error demanding a "Global regions" privacy setting that doesn't exist in the workspace UI. Closed — useful signal on how Go-tier regional/model gating is maturing, and on the friction when error messages reference controls users can't find.

  3. #8689 — [FEATURE]: ability to revert/fork from the ai message, not only from the user's (14 comments, 23 👍) Long-running (opened January) high-upvote feature request: forking conversation state from assistant messages, not just user turns. Persistent engagement over 10 months indicates a real workflow gap in session branching.

  4. #49723 — [2.0] subagents: explore agent denied free tier can only be used from within OpenCode while running inside the CLI (13 comments) The built-in explore subagent fails with a provider-console error even though a general agent with identical models works — and notably the bug report itself was auto-generated by the OpenCode CLI agent. Interesting both as a subagent-gating bug and as a demonstration of agent-driven triage.

  5. #52941 — [reproduced] desktop: file tree and preview pane show stale file contents after agent edits (10 comments) Marked reproduced: after agent tool edits, the Review pane doesn't list new files and open previews keep showing old content even after tab close/reopen. A trust-eroding bug for anyone reviewing agent changes in the desktop app.

  6. #58406 — [FEATURE]: add a SearXNG web search provider (7 comments) Requests a self-hosted metasearch provider alongside exa/tavily/firecrawl/parallel/tinyfish — the only way to get web search with no third-party dependency. Fits the pattern of users wanting privacy-preserving, self-hostable options in the provider stack.

  7. #61503 — [CLOSED] OAuth Callback loopback connection refused / Timeout on Linux during ChatGPT Sign-in (6 comments) Browser auth completes at OpenAI but the 127.0.0.1/callback handler on Linux never catches it. Closed after triage; relevant to ongoing auth/delegation work (see PR #61812).

  8. #61511 — [triaging] agent: Crouton Alpha stalls mid-turn and does not continue next steps (6 comments) Agent halts after a few tool calls on multi-step tasks until nudged. Combined with #61502 (Crouton Alpha Free failing on a missing safety_identifier), this model appears to be the current rough edge in the Go/free lineup.

  9. #60268 — [reproduced] tui: escape sequences split across reads are typed into the prompt (4 comments) A leading ESC arriving in a separate read is interpreted as a keypress and the remainder lands as literal text in the prompt — garbage input triggered by mouse reports and PageUp. Classic terminal-input edge case; reproduced, so a fix should be tractable.

  10. #61827 — go: deepseek-v4.1-flash image rejection bricks sessions (2 comments) Reading six PNGs during a UI-verification loop renders a long-running session permanently unusable — every subsequent request fails on "image input is not available on this engine." The "bricked session" failure mode (no recovery path) is the concerning part.

Also worth noting: vana30421-cpu filed a series of overlapping free-tier reports (#61782, #61740, #61495, #61479) about Windows desktop losing limits while mobile works — closed as pending-close/triaging, but the platform-specific pattern may deserve consolidation into #59387.

Key PR Progress

  1. #61812 — fix(app): drive the voice call lifecycle from one state machine Replaces scattered status patches and ended/ready/joining booleans in call.ts/context.tsx with a single call-machine.ts. Foundation for #61813 (voice reply announcements).

  2. #61813 — fix(app): announce voice session replies from a state machine instead of a 1s poll Stacked on #61812; removes the dirty/watching/setInterval polling pattern. Practical latency and correctness win for voice users.

  3. #61825 — [contributor] feat(core): one registry for feature flags, on by default in dev builds Collapses flags previously defined in four places into one table, off in releases. Infrastructure that should make experimental features cheaper to ship and reason about.

  4. #61826 — [contributor] feat(core): a switch that turns every feature flag on Stacked on #61825: lets users on released builds opt into enabling all flags locally — a direct response to flags being dev-only.

  5. #61703 — [contributor] feat(core): use freeform tool input on models that support it Core now honors the freeform input formats in models.dev instead of forcing JSON strings — e.g. patch can accept a raw patch when the model supports it. Quality-of-life improvement for tool-calling fidelity.

  6. #61835 — [contributor] feat(sdk): read a result for the exact prompt you sent Prompt responses now return a typed input ID resolving to terminal status, error, usage, cost, and last assistant message ID — replacing session-wide idle notification with per-prompt results. Important for SDK consumers building programmatic workflows.

  7. #61818 — fix(app): reread a workspace file changed during its read Fixes a lost-change race by replacing loose flags/inflight map/module-global LRU in workspaces/files with an explicit content state machine. Directly related in spirit to #52941 (stale files after edits).

  8. #61814 — fix(app): reload a file tree directory changed during its listing Queues one follow-up listing when a forced/watcher reload arrives mid-listing, instead of joining the in-flight read and silently missing created/deleted files. The other half of the stale-file-pane story.

  9. #61532 — fix(core): report true exit codes from PowerShell shell commands (closes #61529) Windows shell tool pipes through -Command and wasn't surfacing real exit codes; a longstanding pain point for Windows users relying on the shell tool in agent loops.

  10. #61801 — fix(app): make tab promotion and route-to-tab sync explicit state machines Fixes three concrete tab bugs: closed tabs resurfacing, child sessions opening as top-level tabs, and leaked draft state from racing promotions.

Note: Hona also has a broader batch in flight (#61819, #61793, #61830, #61823, #61821, #61816, #61815, #61809) applying the same state-machine pattern to disclosures, Mermaid rendering, line comments, server dialogs, and mark-viewed retries — reviewers should expect a sizeable stack to land over the coming days.

Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this digest.

Feature Request Trends

  • Session branching flexibility — #8689 (fork from assistant messages, 23 👍) remains the highest-engagement feature ask: users want non-linear conversation control, not just regenerate-from-user-turn.
  • Self-hostable / privacy-preserving providers — #58406 (SearXNG) continues a pattern of requests for local or dependency-free alternatives in the search/provider stack.
  • Grouped/collapsible UI and disclosure consistency — not filed as issues, but the PR wave around disclosure state machines (#61830) and markdown code rendering (#61821) reflects accumulated UI-fidelity complaints.
  • Feature-flag accessibility — #61826's "turn everything on" switch implicitly answers a recurring desire from released-build users to try experimental functionality.
  • Permission/loop-safety controls — #59339 argues for reviving the doom_loop detector in the v2 permission schema; repeated-tool-call loops running indefinitely is a recurring safety concern.

Developer Pain Points

  1. Free-tier quota bugs remain the #1 support burden. #59387 alone absorbs 280 comments, with sub-clusters: counters that never reset, desktop showing no limits while mobile works (#61782, #61740), and HTTP 429s despite Console authentication (#60935). The pattern of platform-specific inconsistency (Windows desktop vs. mobile) suggests a state/sync issue rather than pure entitlement bugs.

  2. Bricked, unrecoverable sessions. #61827 (image rejection permanently breaks a session) and #61511 (agent stalls mid-turn) represent a failure class where there is no clean recovery path — the user must abandon the session. Expect pressure for session-level reset or graceful degradation.

  3. Stale UI after agent edits. #52941 plus the sibling fixes in #61818/#61814 show that file-tree/preview desync erodes trust in the core desktop review workflow — the very surface users rely on to verify agent changes.

  4. Terminal/input robustness. #60268 (escape-sequence splits corrupting the prompt) and #61109 (commands hanging until Ctrl+C) point to input-handling fragility in the TUI and shell tool, particularly on non-Linux platforms.

  5. Windows-specific quality gaps. PowerShell exit codes (#61532), desktop free-limit discrepancy, and 503/model-picker issues (#61495) cluster into a clear signal that Windows paths receive less testing than macOS/Linux.

  6. Go-tier model edge cases. Missing privacy controls for DeepSeek regional gating (#50155), missing safety_identifier for Crouton Alpha Free (#61502), and image-input rejection on deepseek-v4.1-flash (#61827) indicate the model onboarding checklist needs to cover provider-required request fields and capability mismatches up front.

Digest generated from github.com/anomalyco/opencode activity for 2026-11-05.

Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-11-05

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24 hours, but the issue tracker stayed busy: 50 issues and 50 PRs were updated, with a heavy concentration of TUI/terminal rendering bugs (mintty/ConPTY, Zellij, tmux, Ghostty) and several [prio:p0] data-integrity fixes in pi-durable. A notable contributor cluster around petrroll landed a wave of coding-agent fixes covering line endings, UTF-16/non-UTF-8 handling, streaming reads, and OAuth refresh persistence.

2. Releases

None in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. [#7730] High CPU usage on macOS with long sessions (27 comments, 👍12) — Long-running sessions swing between 50–110% CPU with 600–800MB memory; anecdotally tied to context size. Highest-engagement issue of the day; the longevity/performance of long agent sessions is clearly a core concern. Link
  2. [#10256] Terminal color query replies leak into prompt; BEL opens external editor (mintty/ConPTY) (25 comments, 👍4) — A 0.99.x regression: startup emits raw rgb: sequences into the prompt and the BEL byte spawns the editor. Windows-specific but high-traffic and marked inprogress. Link
  3. [#9656] Mouse wheel scrolls prompt history instead of transcript (Windows + Zellij) (14 comments, 👍5) — Multiplexer-specific input handling divergence; same class of bug as the tmux OSC 52 issue. Link
  4. [#10628] OSC 52 copy swallowed by tmux (no passthrough wrap) (12 comments, 👍6) — Copy-on-select silently fails inside tmux while still flashing "Copied!" — a correctness/trust issue for headless SSH workflows. Link
  5. [#11613] bash tool reports timeout for commands that exited with a real exit code (5 comments) — Pipe inheritance from descendants causes false "timed out" results. Affects agent correctness when interpreting command outcomes; already has a PR (#11813). Link
  6. [#9654] read tool loads whole files even when one line is requested (4 comments) — Requesting a single line from a 128 MiB file can OOM the process. A real scalability hazard for large repos/logs. Link
  7. [#11622] [prio:p0] pi-durable accepts submit({type:"input"}) without content, then faults (4 comments) — Malformed conversation entries persist and the run faults with content is not iterable. P0 data-integrity bug. Link
  8. [#11584] TUI overlay does not cover terminal images (4 comments) — Kitty/iTerm2 image rows punch "holes" through overlays. Deliberate-passthrough design meets real usability gap. Link
  9. [#11808] [untriaged] SIGILL (ud2 after sigaction) in Worker thread, headless linux-x64 (2 comments) — Two long headless runs killed by a deliberate trap instruction at the same offset. A native-crash report that deserves maintainer triage. Link
  10. [#11773] [prio:p0] Upgrade Token Plan branding and gateway setup compatibly (2 comments) — Provider-config migration for Qwen Token Plan (China/International endpoints). Notable as a coordinated vendor-driven change rather than a community bug. Link

Honorable mentions: [#9809] large-paste content lost via getText()→setText() (link); [#10732] MCP OAuth never recovers after origin fallback caching (link).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. [#11811] read/edit handle UTF-16 and non-UTF-8 files without corrupting them — Adds shared file-encoding.ts; edit previously silently corrupted non-UTF-8 files and read showed UTF-16 as garbage. Link
  2. [#11751] edit preserves line endings of untouched lines, diffs before writing — Prevents unintended CRLF/LF rewrites and OOM-after-write; encoding work split into #11811. Link
  3. [#11750] Stream the read tool instead of loading whole files (closed/merged path) — Reported 200 MB log read now bounded by offset/limit rather than tripling memory. Link
  4. [#11813] bash tool reports shell exit code when it times out after the shell exited — Fixes the false-timeout class from #11613; distinguishes "shell exited, pipe held open" from real timeouts. Link
  5. [#11812] Wait for a started OAuth refresh to save before exit — Prevents single-use refresh-token loss in RPC mode; a nasty auth-corruption bug. Link
  6. [#11810] Model selector keeps selection when catalog refresh lands — Background refresh no longer resets highlight to the current model; fixes #9109. Link
  7. [#11757] Do not split surrogate pairs when truncating text — Replaces slice()-by-code-unit truncation that produced invalid UTF-16 (lone surrogates) in grep match lines. Link
  8. [#9350] Fork-free executable lookup in findExecutableOnPath/commandExists — Removes spawnSync("which") and <cmd> --version calls that can deadlock multi-threaded hosts on Android/Termux. Link
  9. [#11696] feat(storage): experimental session replication — Upload/pull session commits via a remote using the Chord outbox and applyBatch; second uploader forks to a new session. Early but significant for multi-device workflows. Link
  10. [#8250] Make subagent progress and failures reliable — Fixes false "done" states, lost failure details, and normal-looking tool results for failed delegated work. Link

Also notable: [#9889] manifest resource discovery glob alignment (link); [#9442] compat.supportsPromptCacheKey for proxies (link).

5. Hot Discussions

Q&A

  • [#11404] Official pi code agent sandbox by Docker? (3 comments, 👍2) — Community member found four sbx/pi* images on Docker Hub apparently built for the Pi coding agent and is asking whether these are official. Worth maintainer clarification on provenance/support. Link

(Only one discussion updated in the window; grouped list is short by nature.)

6. Feature Request Trends

  • First-class provider onboarding: requests for LM Studio with dynamic model loading (#7668), Qwen Token Plan Individual CN (#7847), LongCat native provider (#9308), and provider display names in /model (#11795). Pattern: users want /login-driven, discoverable providers rather than hand-edited models.json.
  • Provider compatibility flags: requiresNonNullAssistantContent (#8063) and supportsPromptCacheKey for proxies (#9442) — demand for finer-grained OpenAI-compat knobs.
  • MCP/auth robustness: MCP OAuth recovery (#10732) and durable input validation (#11622) show a push toward hardening stateful subsystems.
  • Self-update controls: pi update --no-release-age-override (#11614) — enterprise/MDM environments need opt-outs from security-software-triggering behaviors.
  • Terminal/TUI parity: consistent scroll, copy, and image behavior across multiplexers (tmux, Zellij) and terminals (mintty, ConPTY, Ghostty, Alacritty).
  • Containerized/sandboxed deployment: interest in official Docker sandbox images (#11404).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Terminal emulation edge cases are the #1 recurring frustration. Escape-sequence leaks (#10256, #11802, #9332, #9257), multiplexer-specific input routing (#9656), OSC 52 being eaten by tmux (#10628), and image passthrough under overlays (#11584) dominate the comment counts. Users on Windows + multiplexers are hit hardest.
  • Tool correctness under edge conditions. False bash timeouts (#11613), whole-file reads for one-line requests (#9654), silent corruption of non-UTF-8 files and line endings (#11811, #11751), surrogate splits in truncation (#11757), and lost large pastes (#9809). These are trust-eroding because failures are silent or misattributed.
  • Long-session resource growth. High CPU/memory on long sessions (#7730) and worker-thread crashes in long headless runs (#11808) raise questions about soak-testing.
  • Stateful subsystem fragility. OAuth refresh-token loss on exit (#11812), MCP OAuth non-recovery (#10732), invalid durable inputs (#11622), and extension console output corrupting the TUI (#10002) point to lifecycle/ownership gaps.
  • Cross-platform spawn/fork hazards. spawnSync on the caller thread (#11809/#9350) can freeze in-process hosts, especially on Android/Termux — a reminder that sync subprocess calls are unsafe in embedded contexts.
  • Enterprise friction. MDM software flagging release-age overrides (#11614) and undocumented third-party Docker images (#11404) suggest a need for clearer enterprise deployment guidance.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-05

1. Today's Highlights

The project shipped v0.26.7 with an operator-scoped model.catalogRefresh setting and better handling of privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled: false. CI health dominates the conversation this cycle, with "Main CI failed" auto-filed issues flooding the tracker (the top one has 185 comments). Meanwhile, community feature work is converging around provider presets (OCI Generative AI), MCP robustness, and long-context overflow handling.

2. Releases

v0.26.7 (last 24h)

  • Adds an operator-scoped model.catalogRefresh setting.
  • privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled: false now also stops background catalog refresh, aligning privacy controls with network behavior.
  • No known breaking changes.
  • Nightly v0.26.7-nightly.20261104.b9e20830f7 also published (integration test isolation fix for ACP parity runtime state — #16254).

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, no test identified (185 comments) The longest-running CI failure thread. Autofix is skipped, and the comment churn suggests flaky/undiagnosable gating rather than a single defect — a signal that CI triage tooling needs improvement.

  2. #12714 — Main CI failed: Qwen Code CI, no test identified (29 comments) Open since Sept 25; a persistent "no test identified" failure class. High comment count reflects the community's frustration with opaque CI signals.

  3. #15712 — E2E: TUI foreground shell PTY/composer draft ownership (14 comments) A flaky TUI E2E test about PTY bytes and composer drafts. Important because TUI stability directly affects interactive users.

  4. #14104 — SDK Java: HostedShellLifecycleRecoveryIT publicDeletionRecoversOriginalResources (12 comments) Marked ready-for-agent + autofix/approved; resource-recovery correctness in the hosted shell lifecycle matters for managed-agent reliability.

  5. #13749 — feat(mods): Claude Code-style Mod runtime with staged compatibility (7 comments) Proposes a register(on, options) / on(event, matcher?, handler) authoring contract compatible with Claude Code Mods. A significant extensibility proposal with roadmap/hooks-events labeling.

  6. #14025 — Replace ModelStudio onboarding with 千问AI平台 / QwenCloud (6 comments, CLOSED) Official provider onboarding change keeping QwenCloud first in /auth. Closed quickly — likely accepted and moving to implementation.

  7. #16322 — E2E: ACP PreToolUse/PostToolUseFailure context delivery (5 comments) Hook context delivery via ACP is failing in E2E; relevant to anyone building on the tool-hook system.

  8. #16332 — feat(providers): OCI Generative AI provider preset (4 comments) Tier-1 provider preset request following CONTRIBUTING.md; accompanied by docs PR #16345. Shows growing demand for non-Alibaba cloud providers.

  9. #15109 — Desktop: task notifications cannot be enabled (WebView loopback origin) (4 comments) A concrete Desktop UX bug: notification permission denied for the ephemeral loopback origin, making the notification toggle a no-op.

  10. #15327 — tracking(core): unified agent loop behind experimental.unifiedAgentLoop (4 comments, P1) Architectural tracking issue to run every surface (CLI, daemon, web-shell) on one agent loop in packages/core. High leverage for consistency across surfaces.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #11854 — feat: hybrid code mode (tools.mode: direct / code_mode / code_mode_only) Codex-aligned JavaScript exec tool alongside ordinary tools. A major agent-capability change; still open and under review.

  2. #16341 — fix(core): keep follow-up suggestions in Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar Uses Intl.Segmenter for script-appropriate word segmentation, fixing dropped suggestions for non-space-delimited languages. Good i18n fix.

  3. #16331 — fix(core): recognize Ollama context overflow for reactive compaction Extends overflow detection (llama.cpp/TGI/vLLM/SGLang already covered) to Ollama, so reactive compaction triggers instead of stuck sessions.

  4. #16335 — perf(managed-agent): tool publication/read leases off the tenant lock Reduces contention on the tenant output_publication guard for ordinary tool publication — scalability work for multi-tenant deployments.

  5. #16327 — perf(managed-agent): narrow queue dispatch and workspace session creation locks Lock-ordering changes to allow independent selections across workspaces of one tenant.

  6. #16278 — fix(ci): apply apt-mirror probe to release docker lane Moves probe logic into shared .github/scripts/apt-mirror-probe.sh; CI reliability improvement addressing flaky apt mirrors.

  7. #16333 — fix(channels): keep GitHub notifications unread on transient thread errors Prevents missed notifications when GitHub returns 5xx/network/rate-limit errors mid-poll.

  8. #16258 — feat(channels): role-aware action templates for GitHub bound sessions (CLOSED) Adds review / verify / fix roles and boundSessionActions templates — declarative automation for GitHub-bound sessions.

  9. #16299 — fix(core): keep session list titles when transcript is rebuilt Persists titles to a .title.json sidecar so web-shell sidebar names survive transcript rebuilds.

  10. #16345 — docs(providers): document OCI Generative AI under OpenAI-compatible providers Companion docs for the OCI provider request, including Chat Completions and Responses base URLs with Bearer API-key auth.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussion data was provided for this cycle.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Provider ecosystem expansion: OCI Generative AI preset (#16332/#16345) and QwenCloud onboarding (#14025) show demand for broader, official provider coverage beyond the current defaults.
  • Extension/compatibility surface: The Mod runtime proposal (#13749) and unified agent loop tracking (#15327) point toward a desire for a stable, cross-surface extensibility contract.
  • Managed-agent scalability & multi-tenancy: Multiple PRs (#16335, #16327, #16325, #16329) and issue #16320 (per-session SQL cost) reveal sustained focus on reducing lock contention and DB work per resident session.
  • Session management: Session-only model selection in the daemon SDK (#15702) and session title persistence (#16299) reflect demand for finer-grained, non-destructive session controls.
  • Model-serving compatibility: Overflow detection across Ollama/SGLang/vLLM (#16331, #14097) and custom served-model-name docs (#16342) indicate users run Qwen models behind many inference servers.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI signal quality: The dominant frustration is opaque CI failures — "no test identified" issues (#14724, #12714) and provisional/flaky E2E reports (#15712, #16322, #15814, #16046) generate massive comment noise without actionable diagnostics.
  • CI infrastructure limits: GITHUB_TOKEN rate-limit exhaustion from bot workflow bursts (#16188) and qwen-autofix.yml approaching GitHub's 500 KB workflow limit (#15970) show automation infrastructure straining under its own weight.
  • Desktop/WebView platform quirks: Notification permission denial on loopback origins (#15109) and orphaned daemons after Desktop crashes (#14600) are recurring Desktop reliability complaints.
  • MCP robustness: Duplicate tool names silently discarding an entire server with a misleading error (#15741) is a sharp edge for MCP users.
  • Context-overflow fragility: Sessions getting stuck on server-side context limits (SGLang #14097, Ollama #16331) remain a top operational pain for self-hosted deployments.

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-11-05

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 的维护者与贡献者吞吐量极高：过去 24 小时内有 387 个 issue 和 500 个 PR 被更新，其中 194 个 PR 已合并/关闭，并发布了 1 个新的 beta 版本（v2026.11.5-beta.1）。头条功能是引入 “Knowledge Scribes” —— 一套跨 agents、sessions 和 Control UI 构建的一流知识捕获工作流 —— 外加一个全新的 PostgreSQL 支撑的状态平面，标志着向企业级持久化迈进的战略举措。然而，issue 追踪器被 P0/P1 稳定性问题所主导（gateway 事件循环阻塞、Windows 服务不可靠、堆/RSS 失控、prompt-cache 回归），其中若干问题已持续 6–9 周仍未修复。项目显然处于高速开发阶段，但活跃 issue 中未关闭（226）与已关闭（161）的比例，以及 clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr 标签的数量，表明维护债务的积累速度快于清理速度。

活跃度评估：非常高（发布周 + 大量分诊量）。

2. 发布

v2026.11.5-beta.1 — openclaw 2026.11.5-beta.1

亮点：

  • Knowledge Scribes — 新增一流的 知识捕获 和可复用的 “scribe” 工作流，横跨 agents、sessions 和 Control UI。通过六个 PR（#185583、#185637、#185974、#186270、#186455、#187659）交付，归功于 @jalehman。这是本版本的旗舰功能，标志着 OpenClaw 推动向持久、可复用的 agent 记忆工件而非临时会话上下文演进。
  • PostgreSQL 数据平面 — 新增 PostgreSQL 支撑的状态后端。（提供的资料中发布说明被截断；完整的迁移/破坏性变更详情以及任何所需的配置/状态迁移步骤在本数据集中不可用，升级前应对照完整发布说明进行核实。）

运维人员注意事项：

  • 这是一个 beta 版本；使用 2026.10.x 的生产用户应关注后续 2026.11.x 修复，尤其是鉴于历史上伴随小版本升级出现的众多未关闭的状态迁移和插件重新物化 bug（例如 #161921、#162585）。
  • 源数据中未提供明确的破坏性变更列表；将 PostgreSQL 后端和插件状态迁移视为升级风险区域，并在推出前审阅 #161921（state-migrated-no-rollback）。

已合并/关闭的 PR（共 194 个；30 个 PR 窗口中的显著样本）：

  • iOS/Control UI 打磨集群 — #158051（iOS 上 Cloudflare Access 嵌入式 Dashboard，已关闭）、#149321（Ask OpenClaw 旁的 Settings 布局，已关闭）、#144670（插件标签页内边距）、#132196（Sessions 标签页对齐）—— 由 @Patrick-Erichsen 等人进行的持续性 UI 一致性清理。
  • Web UI 稳健性 — #149581/#149169（Markdown 表格滚动性能）、#149981（Control UI 中 IndexedDB 不可用时的恢复）、#168524（Vitest 中单一 Lit 运行时 —— 减少 CI 不稳定的测试卫生）。
  • CI/依赖卫生 — #174510（vitest/vite CVE 升级，已关闭）、#193046（CLI fixture 与 Workshop 迁移隔离），以及来自 @vincentkoc 的若干 fix(ci) 隔离 PR。
  • 依赖/导出清理 — #180693、#179811（来自定时 CI 报告的未使用 Control UI 导出）。

值得关注的进行中功能工作（未关闭 PR）：

  • GitHub 集成 → 插件迁移 — #192349（Plugin SDK host API 扩展）和 #192350（GitHub 仓库集成移至捆绑插件）。这是一次重大的架构重构；#192350 依赖 #192349 先合并。
  • Crabbox / 访客环境 — #193047（“Gateway 限定的访客 Crabbox 环境”）和 #193051（安全：在配置权限被撤销后停止设置）。
  • Boat CI 路由 — #193038（将符合条件的 Linux CI 作业通过 Boat 路由）。
  • QA-lab 契约 — #193020（分离的运行时对等数据契约）。

评估： 平台/插件架构（GitHub 插件迁移、插件 SDK）的功能速度强劲，而已合并工作的很大一部分是 UI 打磨和 CI 卫生 —— 这是一个项目在稳定 2026.11 发布前稳定化的典型特征。

  • 成本/效率痛点（#161208、#182891、#178373、#161277）—— prompt-cache 未命中和每轮 token 开销导致真实美元成本（一位报告者：每次心跳 $0.40–0.95）。这是社区日益增长的关切。

7. 用户反馈总结

痛点（不满）：

  • 升级和重启不可靠，尤其是在 Windows 和 macOS 上 — schtasks 权限错误、卡在“Activating”、macOS 上的 ServiceInspectionError（#170956、#169844、#191944）。多位用户报告需要多次重试（“pas na veel proberen”）。
  • 成本低效 — 心跳和每轮信封重写上的 prompt-cache 未命中（#161208、#182891）；每轮 requester_profile 样板（#161277）；无运行级 token 预算和选择加入的循环检测（#178373）。用户为可避免的 token 支付真实费用。
  • 幻影/重复消息和上下文泄漏 — #151962（来自内部运行时字符串的幻影用户提示）、#149153（最终回复渲染两次）、#165041（会话恢复注入在 UI 中可见）。这些侵蚀了对 transcript 保真度的信任。
  • 静默失败 — #148308（Tailscale 声明静默丢失）、#150822（广告的工具无执行器）、#160610（Discord 尽管 bot 健康却“运行时降级”）。
  • 记忆子系统正确性 — #150635（召回驱逐从不提升）、#176187（KNN 截止时间超限）、#143640（记忆发布阻塞 agent DB 写入）。

积极信号 / 用例：

  • 对多 agent、多渠道部署的强劲需求（Telegram、Discord、WhatsApp、Signal、Matrix、WeChat 桥接均在评论中出现），通常有 3–50 个 agents 和长生命周期会话（一例为 13 天、约 310k token 的会话）。
  • 用户正在推动生产规模配置（35 个 agents、284 MB SQLite 存储、18k 向量），这解释了反复出现的大型状态 bug —— 项目正被远超出业余规模的场景使用。
  • 社区贡献者正在积极提交结构良好、带标签的报告（注意普遍存在的 clawsweeper 自动分诊元数据），表明用户基础参与度高且技术成熟。

净情绪： 挫败感集中在运营可靠性和成本上，被对新能力（Knowledge Scribes、插件生态系统）的热情所平衡。用户显然喜欢该产品，但正遭遇成熟规模下的运营问题。

横向生态对比

跨项目对比报告 — AI Agent 与个人助理开源生态

快照日期：2026-11-05 · 项目：OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw

1. 生态概览

开源个人 AI 助理领域正围绕一套共同架构收敛——多通道网关（Telegram/Discord/Slack/Matrix）、可插拔的工具/技能与记忆后端、委派式多智能体执行，以及桌面/Control-UI 层——但各项目在成熟度与专注方向上差异显著。可以清晰看到三个成熟度梯队：OpenClaw 处于超大规模（11k+ 未关闭 issue，约 1,000 次 PR 事件/天），并怀有企业级野心（PostgreSQL 状态平面、插件 SDK 重构）；一个稳定化梯队（Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw）正在处理迁移或发布引发的回归，为整合版本做准备；以及处于低活跃维护模式的 IronClaw。在所有项目中，社区最主要的抱怨已从“缺少功能”转向运行可靠性、安全隔离与成本效率——这是该品类正从爱好者采用阶段（3–50 个智能体的家庭实验室、庞大的插件树、18 天网关在线时长）迈入生产使用的典型信号。插件生态正成为新兴的竞争护城河：黑客松驱动的目录增长（Hermes）、记忆插件后端（QwenPaw、OpenClaw Knowledge Scribes），以及注册表/市场诉求（ZeroClaw）都指向同一方向。

3. OpenClaw 的定位

规模与参照地位。 OpenClaw 的吞吐量大约比同类项目高一个数量级（每日更新 387 个 issue / 500 个 PR，而其他项目为 10–50；每日 194 次合并）。它实际上是参照实现：11k+ 未关闭 issue 既说明采用规模巨大，也说明作为生态重心的负担。

相对同类的优势：

  • 架构野心领先于领域 — 唯一交付企业级持久化层（PostgreSQL 状态平面）和正式插件 SDK host-API 迁移（GitHub 集成 → 内置插件，#192349/#192350）的项目。同类项目仍停留在基于文件/插件目录的模式。
  • 旗舰差异化 — “Knowledge Scribes”（一等公民的可复用知识捕获）是同类项目无法匹敌的产品级功能；QwenPaw 的记忆插件工作和 Hermes 的 auxiliary.skills_hub 混乱表明同一需求被以更不连贯的方式处理。
  • 贡献基础设施 — 自动化分诊（clawsweeper 元数据）、密集的 CI 卫生和专门的深度剖析 issue 文化，吸引了技术成熟的生产用户（35 个智能体、284 MB SQLite 部署）。

技术路径差异：

  • 更重、更单体化的核心，插件捕获在网关启动时进行——这是其最严重 P0 的直接成因（#160959：大型外部插件捕获阻塞事件循环），这是一种更轻量同类项目可避免的脆弱性模式。
  • 发布节奏采用 beta 优先的次要版本线（2026.11.5-beta.1），伴随状态迁移风险（#161921 state-migrated-no-rollback 阻塞升级）——这是同类项目尚未面临的企业级权衡。

社区对比。 OpenClaw 的用户群生产规模最大（最大的插件树、最长的会话——一个 13 天/310k token 的会话），对成本的要求也最高（prompt-cache 回归 $0.40–0.95/心跳）。Hermes 拥有最高的人均贡献者动能（黑客松插件浪潮、od -c 质量的报告）；ZeroClaw 的反馈者最懂安全；QwenPaw 拥有最强的首次贡献者管道；IronClaw 基本沉寂。

注意事项： OpenClaw 的速度掩盖了维护债务——在其约 20 个最高严重度 issue 中，只有两个有开放的修复 PR。作为参照实现目前既是该项目最大的资产，也是其最大的发布风险（2026.11 稳定版）。

4. 共性技术焦点领域

五项需求在 ≥3 个项目中反复出现，表明存在真正的品类级压力：

6. 社区动能与成熟度

第一梯队 — 超大规模迭代（OpenClaw）。 发布周 + 每日 194 次合并。在稳定 UI/CI 的同时快速迭代平台架构（GitHub-as-plugin 重构、PostgreSQL）。成熟度风险：维护债务积累速度快于清理速度；需要在 2026.11 稳定版切分前为 P0 集群配备专门的深度剖析负责人。

第二梯队 — 通过迁移/发布门禁稳定化（Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw）。

  • Hermes 处于迁移后阶段（统一网关，10 月 14 日合并）：下一个版本承载过高期望（整合 + 迁移指引 + 会话所有权围栏 PR #149055/#149132）。生态动能是本组最佳。
  • QwenPaw 处于干净的 beta 稳定化窗口（2.3.0b2）：大多数高/中回归是 beta 特有的，两个 Windows Hub 修复已在处理中，首次贡献者流健康。有望迎来绿色的 2.3.0 正式版。
  • ZeroClaw 正在为 v0.9.0 做发布门禁，安全关闭有纪律（P0/P1 数据丢失事项在 24 小时内修复）——强烈的健康信号——但 46 个未关闭 PR 带有堆叠的、受评审门禁的依赖，使维护者评审带宽成为吞吐上限。最高结构性风险：3 个月之久的 #9572 无修复。

第三梯队 — 维护模式（IronClaw）。 零 issue，一个 Dependabot 主版本 PR。无回归信号，但也无前进动能；稀疏数据集可能不完整，因此参与度结论置信度低。

头条指标： OpenClaw 的 500 次 PR 更新 vs. Hermes/QwenPaw/ZeroClaw 各约 50 次，确认 OpenClaw 为参照节点，而第二梯队三项目共同代表生态的活跃稳定化与创新前沿（黑客松插件、E2EE、安全加固）。

7. 趋势信号

1. 可靠性是新的功能战场。 每个活跃项目参与度最高的 issue 都是运维性的：升级死锁（OpenClaw #161921）、损坏的状态文件阻塞所有会话（Hermes #145807）、provider-disable 通用错误（QwenPaw #8579）、主体泄漏（ZeroClaw #11198）。对开发者的价值： 将迁移/回滚方案、状态 schema 校验和可操作的错误界面作为一等交付物——静默降级（Hermes #149085/#149107、QwenPaw #8278/#8580）惩罚最重，因为它破坏了人们对智能体基础设施的信任。

2. 信任边界正移入模型的执行路径。 ZeroClaw 的发现——shell 审批可由模型写入的值驱动（#12227），委派工具可逃逸主体作用域（#11198/#12232）——加上 Hermes 的审批超时被误标为拒绝（#130272）和 OpenClaw 的工具被通告但无执行器（#150822），定义了一类新的智能体原生安全 bug——既非传统应用安全，也非提示注入，而是“工具调用边界处的权限混淆”。对开发者的价值： 从第一天起就将主体/权限传播构建进工具执行契约；ZeroClaw 的仅追加事件账本加确定性重放（RFC #10526）是新兴的最强可审计性模式。

3. 成本可观测性是一项未被满足的产品需求。 Prompt-cache 回归和每轮开销正产生真实的美元抱怨（OpenClaw $0.40–0.95/心跳）。对开发者的价值： token/成本预算、缓存命中遥测和循环检测是差异化平台功能，而非优化项。

4. 插件是生态护城河——也是下一个脆弱性来源。 黑客松目录（Hermes）、记忆后端（QwenPaw/OpenClaw）、注册表共存（ZeroClaw #12109→#12216），以及插件 SDK host-API 迁移（OpenClaw #192349/#192350）表明插件生态将是锁定与排除的决定之地。同时，OpenClaw 的 #160959（插件捕获阻塞事件循环）和 #162585（Windows 重新物化撑爆磁盘）警告：插件生命周期隔离——捕获、物化、沙箱化——是为规模而设计的关键子系统，而非事后补丁。

5. 可编辑、可回滚、可重放的会话。 QwenPaw #7997（消息撤回/回滚，参与度最高）、OpenClaw Knowledge Scribes + 分叉通道片段（#158800）、Hermes 会话谱系围栏（#148762），以及 ZeroClaw 的重放 RFC 汇聚于一项需求：用户将智能体对话视为工作区，而非仅追加日志。 对开发者的价值： 对会话状态的快照/截断/回滚原语将成为下一代平台的基本要求。

6. Windows 与受限环境是隐藏的采用税。 持续的 Windows 可靠性集群（OpenClaw #170956/#162585、QwenPaw #8565、ZeroClaw #12119/#12218）、沙箱化 NAS（QwenPaw fnOS #8515）和 Termux（Hermes #149130）表明 Unix 桌面/服务器之外存在显著的真实需求。跨平台服务管理（schtasks、launchd/TCC、AppContainer）在各项目普遍系统性地投入不足——这对任何率先解决它的项目都是开放机会。

方法论说明：健康评分综合自发布节奏、最高严重度 issue 的修复 PR 覆盖率、分诊延迟和贡献者广度。IronClaw 的结论因异常稀疏的快照（1 个 PR、0 个 issue、评论数未定义）而置信度低。

  • #10526 [已关闭，RFC 已接受] — 仅追加会话事件历史与确定性重放 RFC，现由开放 PR #11921 支撑。
  • 合并/关闭的 PR：#11230（对非管理员 principal 扣留会话数据工具）和 #11220（SOP 执行需要管理员权限）——重要的安全遏制工作。

4. 社区热点

  • #10526（15 条评论，已关闭 RFC）— 仅追加会话事件历史与确定性状态重放。今日最大讨论。底层需求：agent 运行的可审计性和可复现性——超越可变对话日志，转向跨运行时、工具回执、成本记录和委托的可信事件账本。
  • #6437（5 条评论，搁置中）— Zulip 频道请求，定位为刚合并的 Rocket.Chat 频道的姊妹项。底层需求：自托管聊天对等性；今日出现了原生实现 PR #12230。
  • #11198（5 条评论，P0）— 委托记忆工具中的 principal 作用域泄漏。底层需求：自有会话/子 agent 的多租户隐私保证。
  • #12109（2 条评论）— 多插件注册表（ZEROCLAW_PLUGIN_REGISTRY_URL 数组）。底层需求：公共 + 私有注册表共存；由开放 PR #12216 处理。

另需注意：PR #11921 是一个非常大的（size:XL）跨领域变更，几乎触及每个子系统标签——鉴于其影响范围，很可能是未来的热点话题。

5. Bug 与稳定性

按严重程度排序，今日新增/更新的 bug：

严重程度 Issue 描述 修复状态
S0 / P0 #11198 委托记忆工具丢失 principal 作用域（数据丢失/安全） ✅ 已关闭
S1 / P1 #12210 Docker 源镜像构建无法加载工作区 ✅ 已关闭
S2 / P1 #9572 调试网关 WebSocket 轮次溢出默认 Tokio worker 栈 ⚠️ 开放，无 PR
S2 / P1 #11579 save_dirty 在未迁移配置上标记 schema_version → agent 消失 ✅ 已关闭
S2 #12119 Windows：shell/skill/coding-CLI 超时只杀死解释器，后代进程存活 ⚠️ 开放
S2 #12228 cron update --agent 报告成功但从未重新分配 agent（今日新增） ⚠️ 开放
S2 #12227 Shell 审批依赖模型编写的 "approved" 值（今日新增） ⚠️ 开放
S2 #12225 glob_search 从不列出工作区外允许根下的文件（今日新增） ⚠️ 开放

显著模式： 今日到达三个新 bug（#12225、#12227、#12228），全部开放且零评论——需要分诊关注。#12227（审批提示由模型控制的输入驱动）是一个安全相关的信任边界问题，尽管标记为 S2，仍应优先处理。#12119（Windows 超时时的进程树泄漏）是 Windows 平台上持续存在的沙箱弱点，无修复 PR。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

v0.9.x/v1.0 候选，按势头排序：

  1. 多插件注册表 — #12109 → PR #12216 已开放。下个小版本的强烈信号。
  2. Zulip 频道 — #6437 → PR #12230 今日开放。可能与其他频道工作一同发布。
  3. 仅追加会话历史 / 确定性重放 — RFC #10526 已接受，PR #11921 进行中——架构上最重要的路线图项。
  4. 长时间运行的 shell 任务，支持异步/同步模式 + 交互式终端 — #11954；早期阶段，可能 v0.10+。
  5. config migrate 中的已退役环境变量警告 — #12221，schema V4 工作的小型后续。

额外相邻信号：转录默认提供商回退 #12198 和 Telegram 媒体回复上下文修复 #12197 表明频道 UX 的持续打磨。

7. 用户反馈摘要

  • 安全与信任是主要痛点。 用户正在发现真实的隔离缺口：委托子 agent 继承所有者记忆（#11198）、SOP 执行无管理员权限（#11220）、"执行的工作不携带调用者 principal" 的工具（#12232），以及模型驱动的 shell 审批（#12227）。这是对租户隔离保证的不满，而非功能缺口。
  • 配置可靠性很重要。 schema 版本标记 bug（#11579）是那种侵蚀信任的静默数据丢失体验——而且它被快速修复，这是积极信号。
  • Windows 上的平台摩擦持续存在（#12119、#12218），表明 Windows 用户群的沙箱和 CI 体验落后于 Unix。
  • 扩展性需求明确且具体：用户想要私有 + 公共插件注册表（#12109）和更多自托管聊天频道（#6437）。
  • CI/构建稳定性吸引了快速修复（#12210、#12218），表明维护者对工作流阻塞的快速响应。

8. 积压关注

  • #9572（自 2026-07-31 开放，P1，2 条评论）— 调试网关 WebSocket 轮次上的 Tokio worker 栈溢出。超过三个月且无修复 PR；间歇性网关中止是严重的稳定性问题。
  • #6437（自 2026-05-06 开放）— Zulip 频道，自 5 月起搁置在积压中；新 PR #12230 是生命迹象，但 issue 本身应被关联和跟踪。
  • #12119 — Windows 超时时的后代进程泄漏；仅 1 条评论，无修复。安全相关的沙箱缺口。
  • #11954 — 长时间运行的 shell 任务；仅 1 条评论，需要维护者界定范围。
  • 今日新增，未分诊（各 0 条评论）：#12225、#12227、#12228——按明显的分诊规范，应在 24–48 小时内标记和分配。
  • PR 审查债务：46 个开放 PR，若干 size:XL 和 risk:high（#12232、#12213、#11266、#11921）。由于审查门控的安全修复堆叠在依赖链中（例如 #11230 依赖 #11225/#11234），维护者审查带宽是进入 v0.9.0 的主要吞吐瓶颈。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-05

Issues: 387 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-04 23:22 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-05

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw shows very high maintainer and contributor throughput: 387 issues and 500 PRs were updated in the last 24 hours, with 194 PRs merged/closed and 1 new beta release (v2026.11.5-beta.1). The headline feature is the introduction of "Knowledge Scribes" — first-class knowledge capture workflows built across agents, sessions, and the Control UI — plus a new PostgreSQL-backed state plane, indicating a strategic move toward enterprise-grade persistence. However, the issue tracker is dominated by P0/P1 stability problems (gateway event-loop blocking, Windows service unreliability, heap/RSS runaway, prompt-cache regression), several of which have persisted for 6–9 weeks without fixes. The project is clearly in a high-velocity development phase, but the ratio of open (226) to closed (161) active issues and the volume of clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr tags suggest maintenance debt is accumulating faster than it is being cleared.

Activity assessment: Very high (release week + heavy triage volume).

2. Releases

v2026.11.5-beta.1 — openclaw 2026.11.5-beta.1

Highlights:

  • Knowledge Scribes — Adds first-class knowledge capture and reusable "scribe" workflows spanning agents, sessions, and the Control UI. Delivered across six PRs (#185583, #185637, #185974, #186270, #186455, #187659), credited to @jalehman. This is the flagship feature of the release and signals OpenClaw's push toward durable, reusable agent memory artifacts rather than ephemeral session context.
  • PostgreSQL data plane — Adds a PostgreSQL-backed state backend. (Release notes truncated in provided data; full migration/breaking-change details and any required config/state-migration steps are not available in this dataset and should be verified against the full release notes before upgrading.)

Notes for operators:

  • This is a beta release; production users on 2026.10.x should watch for follow-up 2026.11.x fixes, especially given the number of open state-migration and plugin re-materialization bugs (e.g., #161921, #162585) that historically accompanied minor upgrades.
  • No explicit breaking-change list was provided in the source data; treat the PostgreSQL backend and plugin state migration as upgrade-risk areas and review #161921 (state-migrated-no-rollback) before rolling out.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs (194 total; notable samples from the 30-PR window):

  • iOS/Control UI polish cluster — #158051 (Cloudflare Access embedded Dashboard on iOS, closed), #149321 (Settings layout beside Ask OpenClaw, closed), #144670 (plugin tab padding), #132196 (Sessions tab alignment) — a sustained UI-consistency cleanup by @Patrick-Erichsen and others.
  • Web UI robustness — #149581/#149169 (Markdown table scrolling performance), #149981 (IndexedDB-unavailable recovery in Control UI), #168524 (single Lit runtime in Vitest — test hygiene reducing flaky CI).
  • CI/dependency hygiene — #174510 (vitest/vite CVE bumps, closed), #193046 (CLI fixture isolation from Workshop migration), plus several fix(ci) isolation PRs from @vincentkoc.
  • Dependency/export cleanup — #180693, #179811 (unused Control UI exports from scheduled CI reports).

Notable in-flight feature work (open PRs):

  • GitHub integration → plugin migration — #192349 (Plugin SDK host API extension) and #192350 (GitHub repository integration moved to a bundled plugin). This is a significant architectural refactor; #192350 depends on #192349 merging first.
  • Crabbox / guest environments — #193047 ("Gateway-qualified guest Crabbox environments") and #193051 (security: stop setup after provisioning authority revoked).
  • Boat CI routing — #193038 (route eligible Linux CI jobs through Boat).
  • QA-lab contracts — #193020 (separate runtime parity data contracts).

Assessment: Feature velocity is strong in platform/plugin architecture (GitHub plugin migration, plugin SDK), while a large share of merged work is UI polish and CI hygiene — typical for a project stabilizing before a stable 2026.11 release.

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment activity:

Rank Item Comments Signal
1 #160959 — Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins (P0, crash-loop, regression since 2026.9.6) 70 🔥 Highest-engagement issue; plugin-capture regression has major operational impact and remains unfixed.
2 #177656 — Native host exec returns shared-state integrity-admission error on 2026.10.5 (P1) 28 Shared-state/admission failures on stable releases.
3 #170956 — Windows slow startup, unclean plugin shutdown, schtasks permission error (P0) 28 Windows reliability cluster; recurring theme.
4 #120385 — Code Mode tool catalog incomplete for cron/memory-flush turns (P2, author-corrected) 25 Long-running issue with revised root-cause analysis; MCP tool visibility gap.
5 #150635 — short-term recall eviction starves dreaming deep phase (P2) 24 Memory/recall subsystem correctness.
6 #166634 — Late reclamation checkpoint failure leaves agent unavailable after crash recovery 23 Crash-recovery durability.

Underlying needs analysis:

  • Plugin/session state integrity is the dominant theme — #160959, #177656, #166634, #161921, #143640, and #190307 all point at the same architectural pressure: the shared-state / plugin-capture / admission layers are fragile under real-world plugin sizes and crash recovery. Users are running production workloads with large plugin trees, and the startup capture path (#144252) was a meaningful regression.
  • Windows and macOS service lifecycle (#170956, #169844, #191944, #163139) — a persistent cross-platform service-management problem; users cannot reliably restart or update.
  • Cost/efficiency pain (#161208, #182891, #178373, #161277) — prompt-cache misses and per-turn token overhead are leading to real dollar costs (one reporter: $0.40–0.95 per heartbeat). This is a growing community concern.

5. Bugs & Stability

P0 / Critical (release-blocking):

  1. #160959 — Gateway event loop blocks for minutes on large external plugin capture (2026.9.6 regression). No fix PR. Highest severity; affects startup and runtime republication. 70 comments, still open after ~5 weeks.
  2. #170956 — Windows managed-service reliability (schtasks, unclean shutdown, slow startup). No fix PR.
  3. #161921 — state-migrated-no-rollback deadlock between doctor --fix and plugins update. No fix PR. Blocks upgrades.
  4. #169844 — Control UI Gateway update hangs at "Activating" on Windows, leaves Scheduled Task disabled. No fix PR.

P1 / High severity:

  1. #177656 — Native host exec integrity-admission error on 2026.10.5.
  2. #154812 — Runaway RSS outside V8 heap → host OOM and shutdown timeout.
  3. #185578 — Heap floor ratchets up (~25 MiB/h) until V8 cap aborts. No fix PR.
  4. #148789 — Model fallback chain exhausts all candidates on harness-level session failure, misattributes error.
  5. #190307 — Gateway restart leaves agents permanently "degraded" (admission timeout). Related fix PR: #193049 (open, ready for maintainer look).
  6. #192141 — Interrupted-turn continuation drops original user message text.
  7. #191401 — Signal teardown hangs forever on unfinished receive (fix-shape-clear, queueable).

Regressions / cross-cutting:

  • #182891 — Prompt cache never reused (cache read dropped N -> 0) — cost regression.
  • #185656 (CLOSED) — zstd transcript archive exceeds Node string limit; regression of #170847 persisted into 2026.10.5.
  • #162585 — Windows plugin source-capture re-materializes plugin into its own node_modules; large npm trees explode linearly (290 MB → 612 MB/24 min). No fix.

Stability summary: Of the top ~20 severity-tagged issues, only two have associated open fix PRs (#190307→#193049; #191401 flagged queueable). The remainder carry clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr, meaning the automated triage found no candidate fix — a meaningful risk signal for the 2026.11 stable cut. The release note for v2026.11.5-beta.1 does not enumerate fixes for the P0 cluster, so operators should not assume they are resolved.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Most likely to land in 2026.11.x (near-term):

  • Claude web_search provider — #192632 (filed 2026-11-04, P3, 9 comments already). Clear request for parity with Gemini/Perplexity providers; small surface area. High likelihood.
  • Opt-in reaction-triggered agent turns — #17840 (since Feb 2026, 8 comments, +1 👍). Long-standing enhancement; plausible as an opt-in flag.
  • Telegram sendDice message action — #137110 (linked PR open). Likely soon.
  • Control UI: browse/fork prior channel-chat segments after /new — #158800. Fits the Knowledge Scribes direction announced in this release.

Medium-term / needs product decision:

  • skills.workshop.allowSandboxedAgents — #91676 (security review needed, 2 👍). Sandbox policy relaxation requires maintainer security sign-off.
  • Active Memory escalation provider plugin hook — #151178 (linked PR open).
  • Plugin hook for post-tool-result content injection — #164355. Extensibility gap; relevant to the plugin-SDK extension work in #192349.
  • macOS/Talk automation admin turns — #139586.
  • Native contributor admission/lifecycle contract — #158921 (closed stale).

Prediction: The 2026.11.x line will likely prioritize provider parity (Claude search), small channel actions (Telegram dice, Matrix media batching #161505) and plugin-SDK extensibility, while larger features (sandboxed skill workshop, memory escalation providers) wait for security/product review. The GitHub-integration-as-plugin refactor (#192349/#192350) is the most consequential roadmap item in flight and, if merged, will materially reshape the extension model.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dissatisfaction):

  • Upgrades and restarts are unreliable, especially on Windows and macOS — schtasks permission errors, hangs at "Activating," ServiceInspectionError on macOS (#170956, #169844, #191944). Multiple users report needing many retries ("pas na veel proberen").
  • Cost inefficiency — prompt-cache misses on heartbeats and per-turn envelope rewrites (#161208, #182891); per-turn requester_profile boilerplate (#161277); no run-level token budget and opt-in loop detection (#178373). Users are paying real money for avoidable tokens.
  • Phantom/duplicated messages and context leakage — #151962 (phantom user prompts from internal runtime strings), #149153 (final reply rendered twice), #165041 (session-resume injection visible in UI). These erode trust in transcript fidelity.
  • Silent failures — #148308 (Tailscale claim silently lost), #150822 (advertised tools without executor), #160610 (Discord "runtime degraded" despite healthy bots).
  • Memory subsystem correctness — #150635 (recall eviction never promotes), #176187 (KNN deadline overruns), #143640 (memory publish blocks agent DB writes).

Positive signals / use cases:

  • Strong demand for multi-agent, multi-channel deployments (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, Signal, Matrix, WeChat bridges all represented in comments), typically with 3–50 agents and long-lived sessions (in one case a 13-day, ~310k-token session).
  • Users are pushing production-scale configurations (35 agents, 284 MB SQLite stores, 18k vectors), which explains the recurring large-state bugs — the project is being used well beyond hobby scale.
  • Community contributors are actively filing well-structured, tagged reports (note the pervasive clawsweeper automated triage metadata), suggesting an engaged and technically sophisticated user base.

Net sentiment: Frustration concentrated in operational reliability and cost, balanced by enthusiasm for new capabilities (Knowledge Scribes, plugin ecosystem). Users clearly like the product but are hitting maturity-scale operational issues.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or under-attended important items needing maintainer attention:

Issue Age Concern
#91676 — skills.workshop.allowSandboxedAgents opt-in ~5 months (since 2026-06-09) Awaiting security review; blocks a legitimate sandbox-extension use case.
#17840 — reaction-triggered agent turns ~9 months (since 2026-02-16) Long-standing enhancement with clear use cases (emoji polling).
#160959 — P0 gateway event-loop blocking ~5 weeks, 70 comments Highest-priority unfixed P0. Regression introduced in 2026.9.6; still no fix PR.
#161921 — state-migrated-no-rollback deadlock ~5 weeks, P0 Blocks plugin updates and upgrades; mutually-blocking commands are a dangerous failure mode.
#162585 — Windows plugin re-materialization explosion ~5 weeks Disk/time blowup on large npm trees; no fix.
#154812 — RSS runaway → OOM ~7 weeks, P1 Host-level outage risk; no fix.
#164355 — post-tool-result content hook gap ~1 month Architectural extensibility gap; relates to plugin-SDK work.
#150822 — Codex children advertise tools without executors (security review) ~7 weeks Needs-live-repro; potential security implications.

PRs needing maintainer look (ready or near-ready):

  • #193049 — fix: config reload during startup admission (P1, platinum hermit, ready for maintainer look). Directly addresses #190307/#161921.
  • #191914 — fix: child-process spawn fails on glibc < 2.31 (P1, compatibility risk) — important for RHEL/CentOS/Rocky 8 users.
  • #191918 — clarify Codex executable launch failures (small, ready).
  • #191517 — iOS native playback recovery (draft, awaiting native acceptance).
  • #192350 / #192349 — GitHub-integration plugin migration (XL, security-review-required, dependency-ordered).

Recommendation: The P0 cluster (#160959, #170956, #161921, #169844) represents the clearest risk to the 2026.11 stable release. Given 194 PRs merged in 24h, maintainer bandwidth is demonstrably high — but the concentration of no-new-fix-pr tags on the highest-severity issues suggests these need dedicated deep-dive owners rather than routine triage. Prioritizing the two ready fix PRs (#193049, #191914) and assigning an owner to the plugin-capture/event-loop regression (#160959) would materially improve release confidence.

Data source: github.com/openclaw/openclaw, snapshot 2026-11-05. Comment/reaction counts as provided; PR comment counts were unavailable in the source data for the sampled window.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — AI Agent & Personal Assistant Open-Source Ecosystem

Snapshot date: 2026-11-05 · Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The open-source personal AI assistant landscape is consolidating around a common architecture — multi-channel gateways (Telegram/Discord/Slack/Matrix), pluggable tool/skill and memory backends, delegated multi-agent execution, and a desktop/Control-UI layer — while individual projects diverge sharply in maturity and focus. Three distinct maturity bands are visible: OpenClaw at hyperscale (11k+ open issues, ~1,000 PR events/day) with enterprise ambitions (PostgreSQL state plane, plugin-SDK refactors); a stabilization tier (Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw) working through migration- or release-induced regressions ahead of consolidation releases; and IronClaw in low-activity maintenance mode. Across all projects, the dominant community complaint has shifted from "missing features" to operational reliability, security isolation, and cost efficiency — a classic sign the category is moving from enthusiast adoption (3–50 agent homelabs, large plugin trees, 18-day gateway uptimes) into production use. Plugin ecosystems are the emerging competitive moat: hackathon-driven catalog growth (Hermes), memory-plugin backends (QwenPaw, OpenClaw Knowledge Scribes), and registry/marketplace requests (ZeroClaw) all point the same direction.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues updated (24h) PRs updated (24h) Merged/closed PRs Release status Health score
OpenClaw 387 (226 open / 161 closed active) 500 194 v2026.11.5-beta.1 shipped (Knowledge Scribes, PostgreSQL backend) 🟡 Yellow — very high velocity, but P0 cluster (4 issues) unfixed 5–9 wks; no-new-fix-pr tags on top-severity items
Hermes Agent 50 50 11 None; v0.22.5 / v0.21.6 current 🟡🟢 Yellow-green — strong contributor energy (plugin hackathon), >1,000 open issues, P1 silent-failure class open
IronClaw 0 1 0 None ⚪ Quiet/stable — maintenance mode; 1 Dependabot PR (zip 8→9 major bump); possible data-snapshot partiality
QwenPaw 10 50 13 (3 issues closed) None; iterating against 2.3.0b2 beta 🟢 Green — good but noisy; 3 High-sev 2.3.0b2 regressions, 2 with fix PRs in flight
ZeroClaw 16 50 4 None; v0.9.0 release gate assembling 🟢 Green (with risk) — disciplined security hardening; 46 open PRs = review-bandwidth bottleneck

3. OpenClaw's Position

Scale and reference status. OpenClaw operates roughly an order of magnitude above its peers on throughput (387 issues / 500 PRs updated daily vs. 10–50 for the others; 194 merges/day). It is effectively the reference implementation: 11k+ open issues signals both massive adoption and the burden of being the ecosystem's center of gravity.

Advantages over peers:

  • Architectural ambition ahead of the field — the only project shipping an enterprise persistence layer (PostgreSQL state plane) and a formal Plugin SDK host-API migration (GitHub integration → bundled plugin, #192349/#192350). Peers are still on file-based/plugin-catalog models.
  • Flagship differentiation — "Knowledge Scribes" (first-class reusable knowledge capture) is a product-level feature no peer matches; QwenPaw's memory-plugin work and Hermes' auxiliary.skills_hub confusion show the same need addressed less coherently.
  • Contribution infrastructure — automated triage (clawsweeper metadata), dense CI hygiene, and dedicated deep-dive issue culture attract technically sophisticated production users (35-agent, 284 MB SQLite deployments).

Divergences in technical approach:

  • Heavier, monolithic core with plugin capture at gateway startup — the direct cause of its worst P0 (#160959: event-loop blocking on large external plugin capture), a fragility pattern the lighter peers avoid.
  • Release cadence via beta-first minor lines (2026.11.5-beta.1) with state-migration risk (#161921 state-migrated-no-rollback blocks upgrades) — an enterprise-tradeoff peers don't yet face.

Community comparison. OpenClaw's user base is the most production-scaled (largest plugin trees, longest sessions — one 13-day/310k-token session) and most demanding on cost (prompt-cache regression $0.40–0.95/heartbeat). Hermes has the highest per-capita contributor energy (hackathon plugin wave, od -c-quality reports); ZeroClaw the most security-literate reporters; QwenPaw the strongest first-time-contributor pipeline; IronClaw essentially silent.

Caveat: OpenClaw's velocity masks maintenance debt — of its top ~20 severity issues, only two have open fix PRs. Being the reference implementation is currently the project's greatest asset and its largest release risk (2026.11 stable).

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Five requirements recur across ≥3 projects, indicating genuine category-wide pressure:

Need Projects Concrete signal
Session/state integrity & crash recovery OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw, QwenPaw OpenClaw #160959/#161921/#166634 (shared-state admission, no-rollback deadlock); Hermes #145807 (corrupted active_sessions.json blocks all sessions), #148762 (dual-profile session IDs); ZeroClaw RFC #10526 (append-only event history + deterministic replay — the architectural answer)
Principal/tenant isolation for delegated tools ZeroClaw, OpenClaw, Hermes ZeroClaw #11198 (memory tools lose principal scope), #11220 (SOP needs admin authority), #12227 (model-written "approved" value); OpenClaw #150822 (tools advertised without executors); Hermes delegated-subagent observability #149110
Silent-failure elimination Hermes, QwenPaw, OpenClaw Hermes #149085 (commands dropped silently), #149107 (fallback model swapped unnoticed), #130272 (approval timeout mislabeled "denied"); QwenPaw #8278/#8579/#8580 (Markdown downgrade, generic "Internal error", tag 503); OpenClaw #148308/#150822

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Tier 1 — Hyperscale iteration (OpenClaw). Release week + 194 merges/day. Rapidly iterating on platform architecture (GitHub-as-plugin refactor, PostgreSQL) while stabilizing UI/CI. Maturity risk: maintenance debt accumulating faster than clearance; needs dedicated deep-dive owners for the P0 cluster before the 2026.11 stable cut.

Tier 2 — Stabilizing through migration/release gates (Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw).

  • Hermes is post-migration (unified gateway, merged Oct 14): the next release carries outsized expectations (consolidation + migration guidance + session-ownership fencing PRs #149055/#149132). Ecosystem momentum is the best in the set.
  • QwenPaw is in a clean beta-stabilization window (2.3.0b2): most High/Medium regressions are beta-specific, two Windows Hub fixes already in flight, healthy first-time-contributor flow. Well-positioned for a green 2.3.0 final.
  • ZeroClaw is release-gating v0.9.0 with disciplined security closures (P0/P1 data-loss items fixed inside 24h) — a strong health signal — but 46 open PRs with stacked, review-gated dependencies make maintainer review bandwidth the throughput ceiling. Highest structural risk: the 3-month-old #9572 with no fix.

Tier 3 — Maintenance mode (IronClaw). Zero issues, one Dependabot major-version PR. No regression signal, but no forward momentum either; the sparse dataset may be partial, so engagement conclusions are low-confidence.

Headline metric: OpenClaw's 500 PR updates vs. Hermes/QwenPaw/ZeroClaw's ~50 each confirms OpenClaw as the reference node, while the Tier 2 trio collectively represents the ecosystem's active stabilization and innovation frontier (hackathon plugins, E2EE, security hardening).

7. Trend Signals

1. Reliability is the new feature war. Every active project's top-engagement issues are operational: upgrade deadlocks (OpenClaw #161921), corrupted state files blocking all sessions (Hermes #145807), provider-disable generic errors (QwenPaw #8579), principal leaks (ZeroClaw #11198). Value for developers: ship migration/rollback stories, state-schema validation, and actionable error surfaces as first-class deliverables — silent degradation (Hermes #149085/#149107, QwenPaw #8278/#8580) is penalized hardest because it breaks trust in agent infrastructure.

2. Trust boundaries are moving into the model's path. ZeroClaw's findings that shell approval can be driven by model-written values (#12227) and delegated tools can escape principal scope (#11198/#12232), plus Hermes' approval-timeout mislabeled as denial (#130272) and OpenClaw's tools-advertised-without-executor (#150822), define a new class of agent-native security bugs — neither traditional appsec nor prompt-injection, but "authority confusion at the tool-call boundary." Value for developers: build principal/authority propagation into the tool-execution contract from day one; ZeroClaw's append-only event ledger with deterministic replay (RFC #10526) is the strongest emerging pattern for auditability.

3. Cost observability is an unmet product requirement. Prompt-cache regressions and per-turn overhead are producing real dollar complaints (OpenClaw $0.40–0.95/heartbeat). Value for developers: token/cost budgets, cache-hit telemetry, and loop detection are differentiating platform features, not optimizations.

4. Plugins are the ecosystem moat — and the next fragility source. Hackathon catalogs (Hermes), memory backends (QwenPaw/OpenClaw), registry coexistence (ZeroClaw #12109→#12216), and the plugin-SDK host-API migration (OpenClaw #192349/#192350) show plugin ecosystems are where lock-in and lock-out will be decided. Simultaneously, OpenClaw's #160959 (plugin capture blocking the event loop) and #162585 (Windows re-materialization blowing up disk) warn that plugin lifecycle isolation — capture, materialization, sandboxing — is the critical subsystem to design for scale, not an afterthought.

5. Editable, reversible, replayable sessions. QwenPaw #7997 (message retraction/rollback, highest engagement), OpenClaw Knowledge Scribes + forked channel segments (#158800), Hermes session-lineage fencing (#148762), and ZeroClaw's replay RFC converge on one requirement: users treat agent conversations as workspaces, not append-only logs. Value for developers: snapshot/truncate/rollback primitives over session state will be table stakes for the next platform generation.

6. Windows and constrained environments are a hidden adoption tax. Persistent Windows reliability clusters (OpenClaw #170956/#162585, QwenPaw #8565, ZeroClaw #12119/#12218), sandboxed NAS (QwenPaw fnOS #8515), and Termux (Hermes #149130) indicate significant real-world demand outside Unix desktop/server. Cross-platform service management (schtasks, launchd/TCC, AppContainer) remains systematically under-resourced across the board — an open opportunity for any project that solves it first.

Methodology note: health scores are synthesized from release cadence, fix-PR coverage of top-severity issues, triage latency, and contributor breadth. IronClaw conclusions are low-confidence due to an unusually sparse snapshot (1 PR, 0 issues, undefined comment counts).

  • [#8234] GBK/CP936 decoding in read/edit/grep — open PR since 2026-10-14 (Under Review, XXL), no recent merge signal; affects Chinese-Windows users' file tools significantly. Link
  • [#8236] Ollama context window from num_ctx — open PR since 2026-10-14 (Under Review, XL); local-model users silently truncate at wrong windows. Link
  • [#8034] Bound inline media per request — open XXL PR since 2026-09-29; multi-megabyte request bodies can break gateways; a latent production stability issue. Link
  • [#8579] Stale provider run-config — newly filed, High severity, no fix PR; should be triaged promptly as it breaks all channel messaging after a routine config change. Link

Digest generated from provided GitHub activity snapshot. Links point to the referenced issues/PRs on github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-05

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw shows a release-gate hardening phase ahead of v0.9.0, with 7 issues closed and 4 PRs merged/closed in the last 24h — nearly all of them security- or CI-related. Activity is high (50 PR updates, 16 issue updates) but heavily skewed toward a security cluster: principal/identity scoping for delegated tools, SOP execution, and gateway bearer verification. Two P1 and several P0/S0 items (data loss / security risk) moved toward closure today, which is a strong health signal. However, the open PR queue is large (46 open), and the project shipped no releases. Overall: healthy and disciplined, but in a high-risk security crunch with a growing review backlog.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24h. The volume of release:v0.9.0-tagged items moving today (see #11198, #11579, #11961, #11230, #11220) indicates v0.9.0 is being actively assembled.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed today (7 issues, 4 PRs), clustered around security and CI hygiene:

  • #11198 [CLOSED, P0] — Delegated memory tools lost principal scope (data-loss/security risk). Fixed.
  • #11579 [CLOSED, P1] — save_dirty wrongly stamped schema_version = 3 on V1/V2 configs, causing agents to disappear after migration skip. Fixed.
  • #11951 [CLOSED] — Gateway WebSocket upgrades failed over built-in TLS listener. Fixed.
  • #11961 [CLOSED] — Dashboard OIDC sign-in feature landed.
  • #12218 [CLOSED] and #12210 [CLOSED, P1] — CI regressions (Windows Clippy full-history fetch timeout; Docker source image build workspace load failure). Both fixed.
  • #10526 [CLOSED, RFC accepted] — Append-only session event history & deterministic replay RFC, now backed by open PR #11921.
  • Merged/closed PRs: #11230 (withhold session-data tools from non-admin principals) and #11220 (SOP execution requires admin authority) — significant security containment work.

4. Community Hot Topics

  • #10526 (15 comments, closed RFC) — Append-only session event history and deterministic state replay. Largest discussion today. Underlying need: auditability and reproducibility of agent runs — moving beyond mutable conversation logs toward a trustworthy event ledger split across runtime, tool receipts, cost records, and delegates.
  • #6437 (5 comments, parking-lot) — Zulip channel request, framed as a sibling to the just-merged Rocket.Chat channel. Underlying need: self-hosted chat parity; a native implementation PR #12230 appeared today.
  • #11198 (5 comments, P0) — Principal-scope leak in delegated memory tools. Underlying need: multi-tenant privacy guarantees for owned sessions/subagents.
  • #12109 (2 comments) — Multiple plugin registries (ZEROCLAW_PLUGIN_REGISTRY_URL array). Underlying need: public + private registry coexistence; addressed by open PR #12216.

Also worth noting: PR #11921 is a very large (size:XL) cross-cutting change touching nearly every subsystem tag — a likely future hot topic given its blast radius.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity, today's new/updated bugs:

Severity Issue Description Fix status
S0 / P0 #11198 Delegated memory tools lose principal scope (data loss/security) ✅ Closed
S1 / P1 #12210 Docker source image builds fail to load workspace ✅ Closed
S2 / P1 #9572 Debug gateway WebSocket turns overflow default Tokio worker stack ⚠️ Open, no PR
S2 / P1 #11579 save_dirty stamps schema_version on unmigrated config → agent disappears ✅ Closed
S2 #12119 Windows: shell/skill/coding-CLI timeouts kill only interpreter, descendants survive ⚠️ Open
S2 #12228 cron update --agent reports success but never reassigns agent (new today) ⚠️ Open
S2 #12227 Shell approval relies on model-written "approved" value (new today) ⚠️ Open
S2 #12225 glob_search never lists files under allowed roots outside workspace (new today) ⚠️ Open

Notable pattern: three fresh bugs arrived today (#12225, #12227, #12228), all open with zero comments — triage attention needed. #12227 (approval prompt driven by model-controlled input) is a security-relevant trust boundary issue and should be prioritized despite its S2 label. #12119 (Windows process-tree leak on timeout) is a sustained sandbox weakness on the Windows platform with no fix PR.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Candidates for v0.9.x/v1.0, ranked by momentum:

  1. Multiple plugin registries — #12109 → PR #12216 already open. Strong signal for next minor.
  2. Zulip channel — #6437 → PR #12230 opened today. Likely ships alongside other channel work.
  3. Append-only session history / deterministic replay — RFC #10526 accepted, PR #11921 in flight — the most architecturally significant roadmap item.
  4. Long-running shell tasks with async/sync modes + interactive terminal — #11954; early stage, likely v0.10+.
  5. Retired env-var warnings in config migrate — #12221, small follow-up to schema V4 work.

Additional adjacent signal: transcription default-provider fallback #12198 and Telegram media reply-context fixes #12197 indicate ongoing polish on channel UX.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Security & trust is the dominant pain point. Users are finding real isolation gaps: delegated subagents inheriting owner memory (#11198), SOP execution without admin authority (#11220), tools that "do work that does not carry the caller's principal" (#12232), and model-driven shell approval (#12227). This is dissatisfaction with tenant isolation guarantees, not feature gaps.
  • Config reliability matters. The schema-version stamping bug (#11579) is the kind of silent data-loss experience that erodes trust — and it was fixed quickly, which is a positive.
  • Platform friction on Windows persists (#12119, #12218), suggesting a Windows user base whose sandbox and CI experience lags Unix.
  • Extensibility demand is clear and concrete: users want private + public plugin registries (#12109) and more self-hosted chat channels (#6437).
  • CI/build stability attracted rapid fixes (#12210, #12218), suggesting fast maintainer response to workflow blockers.

8. Backlog Watch

  • #9572 (open since 2026-07-31, P1, 2 comments) — Tokio worker stack overflow on debug gateway WebSocket turns. Over three months old with no fix PR; an intermittent gateway abort is a serious stability concern.
  • #6437 (open since 2026-05-06) — Zulip channel, parked in the backlog since May; the new PR #12230 is a sign of life, but the issue itself should be linked and tracked.
  • #12119 — Windows descendant-process leak on timeout; only 1 comment, no fix. Security-relevant sandbox gap.
  • #11954 — long-running shell tasks; only 1 comment, needs maintainer scoping.
  • New today, untriaged (0 comments each): #12225, #12227, #12228 — should be labeled and assigned within 24–48h per apparent triage norms.
  • PR review debt: 46 open PRs, several size:XL and risk:high (#12232, #12213, #11266, #11921). With review-gated security fixes stacked in dependency chains (e.g., #11230 depended on #11225/#11234), maintainer review bandwidth is the main throughput bottleneck heading into v0.9.0.

item.content:encoded:
AI 基础设施日报 2026-11-05

生成时间: 2026-11-04 23:22 UTC | 覆盖项目: 6 个

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

横向对比

跨项目对比报告 — AI 基础设施文摘

日期：2026-11-05 | 面向基础设施工程师与技术决策者

1. 生态概览

当前格局呈现出一个处于张力之中的双层市场。高吞吐服务引擎（vLLM、SGLang）正处于加固阶段：没有发布新版本，但成熟度正受到严重正确性缺陷的考验——P/D 分离架构中的跨请求 KV 污染、Mooncake 路径中静默的 KV 页步长损坏，以及多模型发布标签回归。与此同时，本地/边缘运行时（llama.cpp）发布了其 v0.9.0 内核级版本（flash_attn_ext_rows、FP8 E4M3），而网关（LiteLLM）与训练（Unsloth）层则分别聚焦于计费/流式正确性与CUDA 图解码加速。贯穿全部五个项目的共同主线是：推理模型行为以及 P/D + 缓存基础设施正是故障集中的地方，而对于生产部署而言，正确性——而非原始吞吐——才是主导性风险。

2. 活动对比

项目 层级 Issue 活动 PR 活动 发布状态（24 小时）
vLLM 服务引擎 高——以 DeepSeek-V4/V4.1、Qwen3.8 引入为主；1 个 CRITICAL 未修复缺陷 活跃——性能 PR（KV 校验和、Triton 向量化）、模型组合 无发布。 v0.32.0 被标记为有风险（三重回归）
SGLang 服务引擎 高（61 条更新） 极高（500 条更新）——PR 吞吐量最大 无发布。 FlashInfer 0.7.3 迁移进行中（破坏性）
llama.cpp 本地运行时 中等——Intel GPU 回归集群 活跃——后端调优（OpenCL、Vulkan、HIP） v0.9.0 已发布（b12110+）：FP8 E4M3、flash_attn_ext_rows、4 种架构
Ollama 本地运行时 / 分发 高——v0.40.13/14 上的工具调用 + API 正确性回归 中等——工具结果处理、SSE 刷新的修复 PR 无发布。 CUDA v13 语法崩溃（Xid 79）是最高严重级别的未决项
LiteLLM 网关 极高——流式/计费正确性占主导 活跃——9 个 PR 的“控制平面”技术栈正在评审中 3 个发布： v1.108.0（稳定）、v1.106.7（补丁）、v1.109.0-rc.1——均经 cosign 签名
Unsloth 微调 / 训练 中等——桌面/Studio 回归 活跃——CUDA 图解码、多 GPU 扩散 v0.1.915-beta（Qwen3.8-Flash-Next、Glass 主题）

解读： LiteLLM 发布最活跃（3 个发布，均以签名为门槛）；llama.cpp 与 Unsloth 发布了有意义的版本升级；两个重量级服务引擎则毫无发布——两者都在消化破坏性迁移或修复关键正确性缺陷。SGLang 的 PR 数量（500）远超其他所有项目，表明进行中的重构异常繁重。

3. 模型支持竞赛

模型 / 架构 vLLM SGLang llama.cpp Ollama Unsloth
DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 ✅ 引入进行中（但缺少 SM8x；v0.32.0 上 block-size 损坏） ✅ TRTLLM 稀疏 MLA、FP8 KV 布局 — — —
Qwen3.8 系列（2.4T-A95B、Flash-Next） ✅ AMD gfx950 跟踪器 + 优化 ✅ HiCache 备份（含已知缺陷 #48145） — — ✅ Flash-Next 已进入 v0.1.915-beta
Kimi K3.1 Pro / K3 ✅ 广泛的 PR（ROCm、投机解码、Rust、Mooncake/NIXL） ✅ PCP KV 分片 + HiCache + DFlash — — —
GLM-5.2 / 5.3 ✅ 优化跟踪器 ✅ 可中断 prefill CUDA 图 — — —
Mistral Large 4 — — ✅ v0.9.0 — —
Clover / Limite / Metis-1.6 — — ✅ v0.9.0（4 种架构） — —
Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming 🔶 已请求（#47455） — — — —
Drama-3 TTS — — ✅ 音频支持（b12116） — —
Inception Mercury（扩散 LLM） — — — — ✅ 预设 + 实时流式
Qwen3 / 3.5（YaRN、RoPE） — — — ✅ MLX YaRN 缩放 —

谁领先：

  • 服务引擎（vLLM、SGLang）深陷一场前沿模型军备竞赛——两者都在同一批新旗舰模型（DeepSeek-V4、Qwen3.8、Kimi K3、GLM-5.x）上竞速。vLLM 在硬件后端广度上领先（ROCm、Rust 前端、Mooncake/NIXL）；SGLang 在深度架构集成上领先（TRTLLM 稀疏 MLA、PCP KV 分片）。
  • llama.cpp 占据了长尾架构采纳的细分领域——单个版本中新增 4 种架构 + 音频 + 新的稠密/三值模型。它显然是模型格式覆盖广度上的领先者。
  • Unsloth 是微调预设跟进最快的——针对新的扩散 LLM 与 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next。
  • 差距信号： vLLM 对 DeepSeek-V4 的 Ampere（SM8x）支持仍未决（#50576）——这对成本敏感型集群而言是一项有意义的容量规划约束。

4. 性能前沿

优化努力集中在 KV 缓存与分离架构上，内核与量化紧随其后。各层努力分布如下：

KV 缓存与 P/D 分离（活动最频繁、风险最高）：

  • vLLM：连接器无关的 KV 校验和（#62211）、MooncakeConnector RFC、调度器停顿消除（1.0–1.8s）。
  • SGLang：Mooncake 页步长修复、Kimi-K3 PCP KV 分片、HiCache 主机层工作——但这里也正是最危险缺陷的所在（静默损坏）。
  • llama.cpp：flash_attn_ext_rows 用于高效统一 KV 多序列服务——一项基础原语。

内核与注意力：

  • Triton KV 槽向量化（vLLM #62113）、gfx950 上的 AITER prefill 注意力（MI350X 上 9.3s → 4.1s，SGLang）、FP8-Q ASM MLA 验证（P90 ITL 6.77ms → 6.18ms，SGLang）、Vulkan Intel prefill FA 内核（llama.cpp）。

CUDA 图与解码循环：

  • Unsloth 的在 generate() 中默认启用 CUDA 图解码（逐位一致，Qwen3-0.6B 上每步消除约 675 个内核）是当下最被低估的收益——对 T4 级消费硬件而言是免费加速。SGLang 将可中断 prefill CUDA 图扩展至交错 CP prefill。

量化：

  • llama.cpp OCP FP8 E4M3（v0.9.0）+ 面向三值/BitNet 模型的 CUDA TQ2_0。vLLM ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 权重-only 嵌入 rebase。Unsloth FP8 + int8 对 bf16 ConvRot 分析（质量差距量化为 LPIPS 0.0865）。

分布式服务与 AMD/ROCm（新兴主题）：

  • 两个服务引擎都在大力投入 AMD gfx950/MI355X——vLLM 的 Qwen3.8 AMD 跟踪器与 SGLang 的 AITER/MLA 收益表明 ROCm 正从“受支持”迈向“已优化”。FlashInfer 0.7.3 移除 MoeAlltoAll 对 SGLang 的 NVLink 单边全对全而言是一次强制迁移。

净结论： 优化 ROI 仍然最高的是 KV/分离架构的数据搬运——但同一区域也正是当下最严重正确性风险所在。

5. 层级定位

层级 项目 核心功能 主要优化轴 风险画像
服务引擎（集群） vLLM、SGLang 最大吞吐多租户推理、P/D 分离、前缀缓存 KV 搬运、批处理、内核融合、大模型引入 爆炸半径最大——单个缺陷（KV 污染、损坏）影响众多租户；关键数据泄漏类别
本地运行时 llama.cpp、Ollama 单节点/边缘推理、GGUF 分发、消费级硬件 架构覆盖、量化格式、后端内核（OpenCL/Vulkan/Hexagon） 非 NVIDIA 后端上的正确性（Intel Vulkan 非确定性）；Ollama 额外带来分发/工具面
网关 LiteLLM 多提供商路由、计费、配额、护栏、可观测性 用量核算的正确性、流式/回退语义、集群控制平面 计费/配额正确性——静默成本缺口；agent 循环 UX 回归
训练 / 微调 Unsloth LoRA/QLoRA 微调、扩散模型训练、预设 解码内核捕获、内存占用、检查点兼容性 训练数据损坏（S3 manifest 缺陷）与框架重命名漂移

面向决策者的关键区别：

  • vLLM 与 SGLang 是同一层级上相互竞争的替代品——vLLM 在硬件广度与生态（Rust 前端、NIXL）上领先，SGLang 在深度模型专属内核集成与 AMD 确定性上领先。二者之间的选择日益意味着选择一种发布节奏与缺陷面画像。
  • llama.cpp 与 Ollama：llama.cpp 是引擎；Ollama 是构建于其上的分发 + API + UX 层。Ollama 的许多回归（工具调用、Responses API）是它自身的管道问题，而非 llama.cpp。
  • LiteLLM 是本组中唯一的控制平面层，也是今天唯一发布稳定版本的项目——反映出一种不同的成熟阶段（运营稳定性 vs 前沿模型追逐）。
  • Unsloth 位于上游（模型创建），并日益与服务（CUDA 图解码、浏览器 agent）重叠——关注这一融合。

6. 趋势信号 — 值得关注什么

趋势 1 — P/D 分离在设计上已生产就绪，但在正确性上尚未。 两个服务引擎在分离式 KV 路径中都有严重、静默失败的缺陷：vLLM 跨请求污染（#61160，数据泄漏类别）与 SGLang Mooncake 步长损坏（#48230）。关注： --no-enable-prefix-caching 式缓解措施是否会成为标准默认值。*Agent/应用开发者：*若运行 P/D，在 #61160 落地前禁用前缀缓存并审计路由器版本（#31206 dead-prefill）。

趋势 2 — “发布标签回归”问题十分尖锐。 vLLM v0.32.0 有三重回归；Ollama v0.40.13/14 破坏了原生工具调用。关注： 锁版本纪律。应用开发者：最安全的版本往往是**上一个版本（vLLM v0.31.1 是长上下文 Qwen 的推荐锁定版本）。把锁版本内建到部署中，而不是寄望于运气。

趋势 3 — 推理模型对流式栈的每一层都构成压力。 LiteLLM 的流式推理回退缺陷（#49795）、SGLang 的 EAGLE PD 解码损坏，以及 vLLM 的推理解析器空白字符缺陷都源于推理 token 处理。关注： SGLang 新的首答案 token 时间直方图（#48466）——它将推理延迟与答案延迟分离，是面向推理 SLO 的正确可观测性原语。采纳它。

趋势 4 — AMD/ROCm 正从“受支持”毕业为“已优化”。 gfx950/MI355X 出现在 vLLM（Qwen3.8 跟踪器）、SGLang（AITER、MLA）、llama.cpp（HIP fast-math）中。关注： 对于受监管/可复现性工作负载，SGLang 的确定性模式 AITER prefill值得注意。对于容量规划，AMD 在特定模型上现在已是可信的 Hopper/Blackwell 替代方案。

趋势 5 — 网关 ↔ agent 循环互操作性脆弱。 LiteLLM 的 server_tool_use 当作待处理工具调用（#48384）、丢弃加密推理（#49046），以及 Ollama 的工具模板 JSON 损坏（#19529）都会破坏 Claude-Code 风格的 agent 客户端。关注： 工具调用 ID 匹配（Ollama #18767）与显式解析器锁定（SGLang --tool-call-parser auto 不可靠，#48172）。*Agent 开发者：*切勿在生产中依赖自动检测——锁定显式解析器并在客户端侧规范化工具结果。

趋势 6 — 控制平面整合即将到来。 LiteLLM 的 9 个 PR 技术栈（数据平面注册表 → OCSF 审计 → SIEM 汇聚 → OTel span）指向一个控制平面治理多个数据平面——一个集群管理的未来。目前尚无可用之物，但多集群网关运营者应跟踪 #49655。

趋势 7 — 边缘仍在持续获得免费性能。 Unsloth 的逐位一致 CUDA 图解码与 llama.cpp 的 flash_attn_ext_rows 都能在消费级/边缘硬件上带来无需改代码的收益。*应用开发者：*本地服务正在悄然变快；在为延迟敏感的本地工作负载扩展云容量之前，重新做基准测试。

面向决策者的底线

  • 集群服务： 在 DeepSeek/长上下文场景下对 vLLM v0.32.0 保持观望；在关键 KV 缺陷关闭前禁用 P/D + 前缀缓存。SGLang 提供更深的 AMD 确定性，但承载更多进行中的破坏性迁移（FlashInfer 0.7.3、api.v1）。
  • 边缘/本地： 将 llama.cpp 升级至 v0.9.0（验证 FP8 E4M3）；收紧 -hf 量化标签；分类器避免使用 Intel Vulkan coopmat。
  • 网关： v1.108.0 稳定，以 cosign 验证作为契约——但不要信任已中止流的用量计数，并锁定模型 ID（移除 EU Haiku 配置是一个现实存在的隐患）。
  • 训练： 在检查点重命名被消化之前锁定 transformers <5.23；审计 S3/音频 manifest 的静默数据损坏。

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM 文摘 — 2026-11-05

1. 今日亮点

过去 24 小时内没有新版本发布，但 issue 动态主要围绕 DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 和 Qwen3.8 级模型的接入，同时在 SM120（Blackwell）和 P/D 分离部署上出现了若干正确性回归。前缀缓存 P/D 配置中一个可能严重的 KV 缓存跨请求污染 bug（#61160）仍未关闭，而新的性能 PR 则聚焦于 KV 传输校验和 Triton attention 向量化。AMD 继续推进 Qwen3.8 系列的 gfx950/MI355X 优化跟踪。

过去 24 小时无新版本发布。开放事项中的相关兼容性说明：

  • GLM-5.3 优化跟踪（与 5.2 相同的 glm_moe_dsa 基础）（#57406）。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 如果你运行带前缀缓存的 P/D 分离，请在 #61160 修复前禁用它。 跨请求串扰属于数据泄露类 bug，而不仅仅是质量问题。
  • 对 DeepSeek-V4 和长上下文 Qwen 部署，谨慎对待 v0.32.0；对于 262K 预填充场景，v0.31.1 是更安全的固定版本，且发布标签上的 block-size 配置已损坏。
